scope: Repository source and current tests only; no hosted run or retired harness evidence

questions.old: Can hosted storage observation stay independent through pool inspection faults?
questions.answer: Host cleanup reads real ZFS/findmnt state and retains its journal on failed inspection. The generated proof test covers unavailable inspection, and the NixOS backup test covers real interrupted cleanup. A hosted split-view pool fault with a separate read-only observer is not demonstrated.
questions.exact_probe: In a disposable NixOS/ZFS VM, fault only the cleanup unit's zfs/findmnt read, independently enumerate GUIDs/local properties and journal bytes, then remove the fault and verify owned-only retry.
proposed_catalog_open_questions: Can hosted storage observation stay independent through pool inspection faults? `(partial: native source/proof histories exist; hosted split-view fault unproven)`

questions.old: Can a real fixture reuse one Restic component snapshot ID across two retained manifests?
questions.answer: Yes for a constructed real Restic repository fixture: backup-operators.py captures a component once and publishes multiple real manifests referring to it, then verifies retained union after prune. Separate coordinator runs have distinct run tags and are not shown to reuse a component ID.

questions.old: Which isolated guest, database, and host sentinels can be restored safely?
questions.answer: The backup NixOS machine restores a private host sentinel and PostgreSQL into an isolated database; real Restic operator tests verify byte-exact files in fresh private targets. A guest disk sentinel needs a disposable Lilly/ZFS guest fixture.
questions.exact_probe: Write deterministic bytes to a disposable guest disk before capture; restore into an isolated target and compare its hash without attaching it to a live guest.
proposed_catalog_open_questions: Which disposable guest-disk sentinel can be restored independently? `(partial: isolated host/database sentinels already exist)`

questions.old: What policy, if any, defines cross-component consistency or RPO? `(partial: sequential capture is confirmed; no global point-in-time or RPO promise was found)`
questions.answer: ADR-0070 explicitly states nominal RPO of thirty minutes plus jitter and capture runtime, with older last-good points possible during outages. It explicitly states independent components have different timestamps and require quarantine reconciliation; there is no global point-in-time guarantee.
questions.proposed_catalog_prose: Describe nominal RPO only with the outage qualification. Keep the property scoped to retained graph/content closure, not cross-component transactional consistency.

questions.old: Is there a repository-provided historical activation/claim command, or can this run only prove isolated restore and a separately staged drill?
questions.answer: The backup CLI has list/inspect/restore and no activation/claim operation. Restore requires an empty private target; the NixOS test restores an isolated database and launches an operator probe. ADR-0070 requires fencing/reconciliation before serving traffic; ADR-0158 leaves historical UID repair unsupported.
questions.proposed_catalog_prose: State the directly observable safety boundary as private restore with no automatic historical authority activation. Treat a fenced mixed-time activation/reconciliation drill as a separate unimplemented scenario, not proof from this CLI.

questions.old: Is a full 4096-worker hosted run feasible without unrelated OS limits?
questions.answer: Both BEAM producer and Rust state cap pending admissions at 4096; a Rust unit test checks the exact boundary. The native VM fixture has a real BEAM producer but no 4096-worker memory/FD measurement or hosted budget.
questions.exact_probe: Keep 4096 BEAM owners alive in the native two-unit fixture, measure memory/FD headroom, independently witness effects, and compare 4097th :unrecorded result to durable IDs and gap marker; repeat hosted only after resource budget is known.
proposed_catalog_open_questions: Is a full 4096-worker hosted run feasible without unrelated OS limits? `(partial: exact Rust bound tested; BEAM/hosted resource envelope unmeasured)`

questions.old: Which fixture retains systemd producer identity while faulting recorder?
questions.answer: nix/verification/tests/machines/otel-request-recorder runs separate sdk-producer.service and overalls-request-sdk.service with real UID/cgroup/process attribution and independent restarts. No equivalent hosted topology is established.
questions.exact_probe: In the proposed hosted topology, check real peer UID, unit cgroup and start identity via authenticated RPC before independently killing either service.
proposed_catalog_open_questions: Can hosted deployment preserve the native fixture's exact systemd producer identity? `(partial: native two-unit fixture exists; hosted equivalent unproven)`

questions.old: Which hosted deployment preserves exact systemd producer authentication while faulting parties independently?
questions.answer: The NixOS machine fixture exercises real separate units, recorder/producer/VM death, checkpoint reopen and a source-built commit-before-reply cut. Its authentication semantics cannot be inferred for a hosted container topology.
questions.exact_probe: Run authenticated producer RPC under the intended hosted unit/cgroup, independently fault recorder and producer, and verify boot/start identity plus the same durable checkpoint across recovery.
proposed_catalog_open_questions: Which hosted topology preserves exact systemd producer authentication while faulting parties independently? `(partial: native NixOS fixture passes this shape; hosted equivalent unproven)`

questions.old: Which hosted fault reaches actual SQLite commit uncertainty beyond process restart?
questions.answer: SQLite WAL FULL commit precedes intake ACK. Current property/native tests cover duplicate intake, SIGKILL/reopen, delivery ACK/replay and poison, but no demonstrated torn or power-loss commit fault.
questions.exact_probe: Use a supported disposable block-backed VM power cut at SQLite commit and reopen, or use a source-built post-commit/pre-ACK cut only for ACK uncertainty; label those scopes separately.
proposed_catalog_open_questions: Which hosted fault reaches actual SQLite commit uncertainty beyond process restart? `(partial: SIGKILL/reopen and ACK replay covered; media fault unproven)`

questions.old: What exact transient SQLite/WAL footprint envelope applies?
questions.answer: The code uses body+512 logical accounting, a 2 MiB reserve, max_page_count on the main DB, 64-page WAL auto-checkpoint, bounded replay/deletion chunks. One 8 MiB native quota stress test measured less than 12 MiB physical footprint; this is not a general physical cap.
questions.exact_probe: Measure allocated DB/WAL/journal blocks through minimum/default quota ingress, replay, expiry, checkpoint and restart; separate observed maximum from any proved bound.
proposed_catalog_open_questions: What exact transient SQLite/WAL footprint envelope applies? `(partial: one 8 MiB native run measured below 12 MiB; no general bound)`
questions.proposed_catalog_prose: Do not claim that physical bytes always fit quotaBytes; the Nix option calls it a logical archive/SQLite budget. Keep accepted-custody/refusal invariant and measured footprint as separate evidence.

questions.old: Can hosted storage enforce recoverable real ENOSPC?
questions.answer: The spool poisons on SQLite write error and logical saturation has real-ingress native coverage. No trace-spool hosted real-ENOSPC test or reopen-after-space-restoration evidence was found.
questions.exact_probe: Place a disposable spool StateDirectory on a small quota-limited filesystem, fill via authenticated ingress, restore space, reopen, and compare all pre-ENOSPC accepted IDs/bytes. Verify hosted storage can reproduce this before transferring the claim.
proposed_catalog_open_questions: Can hosted storage enforce recoverable real ENOSPC? `(partial: no hosted trace-spool ENOSPC fixture found)`
